identification: Strapped pack of roughly 30-35 sawn scantlings/boards, all 50mm thick, mostly about 75-100mm wide with a few wider boards on top, lengths roughly 1.2-1.5m, on bearers. End grain (photo 3 zoomed) shows mixed golden to dark chocolate brown with dark streaks, consistent with Tasmanian blackwood (Acacia melanoxylon). Hand label on top board: 'APPROX .2 M3 CUB METRE KILN DRIED TAS BLACKWOOD ALL 50MM THICK'. Outer faces greyed and weathered from outdoor storage. Volume claim of 0.2 m3 is plausible from the end count (about 6 rows x 5-6 pieces).

viewing_check: Plane or scrape a corner of a few inner boards to confirm blackwood colour and figure (vs myrtle or Tas oak); look for fiddleback; check for end splits, surface checking, borer and sapwood; measure lengths and count pieces to verify 0.2 m3; check moisture (kiln dried should be ~10-12%); see if inner boards are cleaner than the weathered outer ones.
